optional_codes.reason: Personal history of systemic steroid therapy: describes the completed prednisone course, and no instruction requires it. Defensible either way.

unsupported_codes.reason: Other and unspecified hearing loss, the category that holds sudden idiopathic hearing loss: reporting a code from it treats the hearing loss as current. The note documents it as resolved, with a normal audiogram today.
Conductive and sensorineural hearing loss: reports a current hearing loss, and the note documents normal hearing in both ears.

citations.Z09: ICD-10-CM Official Guidelines for Coding and Reporting FY2027, Section I.C.21.c.8: the follow-up codes are used to explain continuing surveillance following completed treatment of a disease, condition, or injury; they imply that the condition has been fully treated and no longer exists; the follow-up code is sequenced first, followed by the history code. Section IV.J: do not code conditions that were previously treated and no longer exist. Here the sudden hearing loss of the left ear was treated with a course of prednisone that ended in April, the provider documents it as resolved and today's audiogram is normal, so the visit is reported as a follow-up examination and the hearing loss is not reported as current.
citations.Z86.69: Tabular List instruction at Z09: use additional code to identify any applicable history of disease code (Z86.-, Z87.-); instruction at Z86: code first any follow-up examination after treatment (Z09). The inclusion term at Z86.6 is 'Conditions classifiable to G00-G99, H00-H95'. Here the treated condition was a disease of the ear.

coder_notes: Z09 is first-listed. Had the audiogram shown that the loss was back, the hearing loss code would replace Z09. This is surveillance after treatment of a specific condition, not a routine hearing examination. Tinnitus and dizziness are denied. The prednisone course ended in April, so no long-term drug therapy code applies.
